title: Main entrance in the north-east
explanation: A north-east entrance is traditionally associated with clarity, openness and a steady flow of energy.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the north
explanation: A north entrance is traditionally considered favourable for opportunity and movement.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the east
explanation: An east entrance is traditionally linked with growth and new beginnings.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the south-west
explanation: A south-west entrance is traditionally considered one of the less favourable entrance placements because this zone is associated with heaviness and stability.
remedy: Keep the entrance well lit, clean and unobstructed. Use a light-coloured door mat and, if practical, place a brass or metal element near the doorway. Structural changes should be planned with a qualified professional.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the south
explanation: A south entrance is traditionally treated with caution in many Vastu traditions, though several acceptable entrance positions exist within the southern side.
remedy: Keep the doorway clean and well maintained. A strong, well-lit door and a simple threshold remedy are commonly suggested. Ask the reviewing astrologer whether the exact position falls in an acceptable segment.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the west
explanation: A west entrance is not universally rejected, but traditional guidance often prefers north, north-east or east entrances.
remedy: Keep the entrance bright and free of clutter. A mirror or reflective surface is sometimes suggested, but placement should be reviewed before installation.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is traditionally associated with fire. An entrance here is often reviewed carefully, although the exact door segment matters.
remedy: Avoid heavy clutter near the door and keep the area cool and well ventilated. A water or earth element near the entrance is sometimes suggested; confirm with the reviewing astrologer.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Main entrance at the centre
explanation: A central entrance is traditionally avoided because the centre of a property is treated as an open, unoccupied zone.
remedy: Keep the central area light and uncluttered. If the entrance cannot be moved, the reviewing astrologer may suggest a traditional correction. Structural changes should be assessed by a professional.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: House faces the north-east
explanation: A north-east facing house is traditionally regarded as open and auspicious.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: House faces the south
explanation: Many traditional texts prefer north, north-east or east facing homes. A south-facing home is common and usually addressed with simple corrections rather than structural change.
remedy: Keep the frontage well lit and tidy. Light-coloured exterior paint and a clean, unobstructed entrance are commonly suggested.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: House faces the west
explanation: A west-facing home is traditionally considered acceptable, though some traditions prefer north or east facing plots.
remedy: Use light colours and good ventilation on the western side. Keep the main entrance clean and well lit.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: House faces the south-west
explanation: A south-west facing home is often reviewed carefully because the south-west is traditionally the heavier, more grounded zone.
remedy: Keep the south-west portion of the plot relatively heavy, closed and uncluttered. The reviewing astrologer can suggest traditional corrections; structural changes need professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is traditionally the fire zone and is the most commonly recommended kitchen placement.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally associated with water and calm. Placing the kitchen fire here is considered a significant mismatch in many traditions.
remedy: Keep the kitchen clean, well ventilated and free of standing water. Avoid storing heavy items in the north-east. If moving the kitchen is not practical, the reviewing astrologer can suggest traditional remedies.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen in the north
explanation: The north is traditionally linked with water and income. A kitchen here is often reviewed because fire and water are placed together.
remedy: Keep the cooking area separate from water storage and ensure strong ventilation. The reviewing astrologer may suggest a traditional correction.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen in the south-west
explanation: The south-west is traditionally the earth zone. A kitchen here is often considered less ideal than the south-east.
remedy: Keep the cooking area well lit and ventilated. Avoid clutter and ensure the stove is kept clean; the reviewing astrologer can add a traditional remedy.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen at the centre
explanation: The centre of a home is traditionally kept open and unoccupied. A kitchen in the centre is considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the central area as light and open as possible. Ensure strong ventilation and cleanliness. Structural changes should be planned with a qualified professional.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Kitchen and toilet share a direction
explanation: Traditional guidance generally prefers the kitchen and toilet to be kept apart. When both are reported in the same direction, the reviewer should confirm whether they are actually adjacent.
remedy: Keep doors closed, maintain strong ventilation, and separate the two areas with a physical barrier if possible. Confirm the exact layout with the reviewer before making changes.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Master bedroom in the south-west
explanation: The south-west is traditionally considered the best zone for the master bedroom because it supports stability and groundedness.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Master bedroom in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally kept light and open. Placing the master bedroom here is considered a significant mismatch in many traditions.
remedy: Keep the room light, uncluttered and well ventilated. Avoid heavy furniture in the north-east corner. The reviewing astrologer can suggest a traditional remedy.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Master bedroom in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is traditionally the fire zone. A master bedroom here is often reviewed because rest and fire are seen as different qualities.
remedy: Use calm, cool colours and keep the room free of clutter. Good ventilation and light-blocking curtains are commonly suggested.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Master bedroom at the centre
explanation: The centre of the home is traditionally kept open. A bedroom in the centre is considered a Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the central space as open and light as possible. Avoid heavy storage in the middle of the home. Discuss any structural change with a professional.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Toilet in the north-west
explanation: The north-west is one of the commonly recommended zones for toilets and bathrooms in traditional Vastu.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Toilet in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally treated as a sacred, light zone. A toilet here is considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the area dry, clean and well ventilated. Close the toilet lid and door when not in use. The reviewing astrologer may suggest a traditional correction.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Toilet in the east
explanation: The east is traditionally associated with growth and openness. A toilet here is often reviewed carefully.
remedy: Keep the area dry and well ventilated, and close the door when not in use. Avoid storing cleaning chemicals openly.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Toilet in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is traditionally the fire zone. Combining it with a water-heavy toilet is often reviewed.
remedy: Keep the toilet dry and well ventilated. Use a simple earth or metal accent if the reviewer suggests it, and avoid heavy clutter.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Toilet at the centre
explanation: A toilet in the centre of the home is traditionally considered a serious Vastu concern because the centre is kept open.
remedy: Keep the area spotless, dry and well ventilated. Keep the door closed and consider a simple traditional correction suggested by the reviewer. Structural changes need professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Bathroom in the north-west
explanation: The north-west is one of the commonly recommended zones for bathrooms in traditional Vastu.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Bathroom in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally kept light and sacred. A bathroom here is considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the bathroom dry, clean and well ventilated. Close the door when not in use and avoid heavy storage in the north-east corner.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Bathroom at the centre
explanation: A central bathroom is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern because the centre is kept open.
remedy: Keep the area completely dry and clean. Close the door and use good ventilation. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction before changing fixtures.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Prayer room in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is the most commonly recommended direction for a prayer or meditation room.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Prayer room in the east
explanation: An east-facing prayer room is traditionally considered favourable.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Prayer room in the south
explanation: Traditional guidance usually prefers the north-east, north or east for a prayer room. The south is often reviewed carefully.
remedy: Keep the space clean, quiet and well lit. Face north or east while praying if the room orientation allows it.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Prayer room in the south-west
explanation: The south-west is traditionally associated with grounded, heavy energy, while a prayer room is usually placed in a light zone.
remedy: Keep the room uncluttered and well lit. A north-east lamp or a small open space can be added if the reviewer agrees.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Prayer room in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is the fire zone. A prayer room here is sometimes accepted, but many traditions prefer the north-east.
remedy: Keep the space calm and free of clutter. Soft lighting and a clean altar are commonly suggested.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Staircase in the south-west
explanation: The south-west, south and west are commonly recommended for staircases in traditional Vastu.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Staircase in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally kept light and open. A staircase here is considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the area under and around the stairs clean and uncluttered. Avoid heavy storage in the north-east. Discuss structural changes with a professional.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Staircase at the centre
explanation: A staircase in the centre of the home is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern because the centre is kept open.
remedy: Keep the central area as open and light as possible. Avoid storing heavy items beneath the stairs. Structural changes need professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Staircase in the south-east
explanation: The south-east is the fire zone. A staircase here is often reviewed, although the exact position matters.
remedy: Keep the staircase well lit and free of clutter. Avoid open storage under the stairs if possible.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Overhead water tank in the south-west
explanation: An overhead tank in the south-west or west is commonly recommended so the heavier element stays in the heavier zone.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Overhead water tank in the north-east
explanation: A heavy overhead tank in the north-east is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern because the north-east is kept light.
remedy: Keep the tank well maintained and free of leaks. If relocation is not practical, the reviewer may suggest a traditional correction. Structural changes need professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Overhead water tank at the centre
explanation: A heavy tank over the centre of the home is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the area under the tank dry and uncluttered. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction; moving the tank needs professional assessment.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Underground water tank in the north-east
explanation: An underground tank in the north-east or north is commonly recommended in traditional Vastu.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Underground water tank in the south-west
explanation: An underground tank in the south-west is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern because water is placed in the heavy, stable zone.
remedy: Keep the area dry and well drained. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction before any excavation or structural work.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Septic tank in the north-east
explanation: The north-east is traditionally kept clean and open. A septic tank here is considered a significant Vastu concern.
remedy: Keep the area clean, covered and free of leaks. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction; relocation needs professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Septic tank in the south-west
explanation: A septic tank in the south-west is traditionally considered a significant concern because the south-west is kept stable and heavy.
remedy: Keep the tank covered and free of leaks. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction; relocation needs professional advice.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Regular plot shape
explanation: A square or rectangular plot with clear corners is traditionally preferred for balanced Vastu.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Irregular plot shape
explanation: An irregular plot can leave some zones extended or cut away. Traditional Vastu often reviews the effect of each missing or extended corner.
remedy: Keep the plot boundaries clean and clearly marked. The reviewer may suggest a traditional correction based on which corner is irregular.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Triangular plot
explanation: A triangular plot is traditionally considered a significant Vastu concern because the shape leaves sharp, cut-away zones.
remedy: Keep the sharp corners clean and, if possible, use them for non-living functions. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction before construction or major changes.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Plot opens to the north-east
explanation: A plot opening towards the north-east is traditionally considered favourable.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Plot opens to the south-west
explanation: A south-west opening is often reviewed carefully because the south-west is traditionally the heavy, enclosed zone.
remedy: Keep the south-west boundary relatively solid and uncluttered. Ask the reviewer for a traditional correction before changing the plot orientation.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Road on the north or east side
explanation: A road on the north or east side is traditionally considered favourable for movement and opportunity.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: T-junction facing the property
explanation: A road ending directly at the property is traditionally treated as a significant Vastu concern. The exact angle and distance matter, so the reviewer should confirm it from the map.
remedy: Keep the facing wall clean and unobstructed. A planter or a low barrier is sometimes suggested. The reviewer should verify the junction from the map before recommending anything structural.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Property at the end of a dead-end road
explanation: A dead-end location is often reviewed in traditional Vastu because movement and access are limited. It is not automatically a serious concern.
remedy: Keep the approach to the property well lit and unobstructed. The reviewer can confirm whether the exact position is acceptable.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Road on the south-west side
explanation: A road along the south-west side is sometimes reviewed because the south-west is traditionally kept heavier and more enclosed.
remedy: Keep the south-west boundary well maintained and avoid an open, unguarded passage there. The reviewer can confirm whether the road actually touches this side.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Intersection in the north-east
explanation: A north-east intersection is traditionally considered favourable.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Intersection in the south-west
explanation: A south-west intersection is often reviewed because the south-west is traditionally the heavier zone.
remedy: Keep the south-west boundary clean and well maintained. The reviewer should confirm the exact intersection from the map.
source: Common traditional Vastu guidance; local traditions vary.

title: Five-element coverage is incomplete
explanation: Using a common traditional direction-to-element mapping, two or more elements are not represented by any of the reported zones.
remedy: This is an informational traditional observation, not a defect. The reviewer can suggest simple element accents only if they fit the home's actual layout.
source: Common traditional Vastu mapping; traditions differ and this is not a scientific measure.
